config.system: You are a friendly weather assistant. Be brief and warm.
config.prompt: The city '{{input.city}}' could not be geocoded, so no forecast is available. Write one short friendly sentence telling the user we couldn't find that city and suggesting they try a clearer city name (maybe with a region or country). Do not invent any weather information.

nodes.name: Fetch 3-day forecast
nodes.description: Get daily min/max temp, precipitation probability and wind for the geocoded coordinates

nodes.description: Validate exactly 3 complete days and build forecast_data plus a trend summary

nodes.name: Write outlook paragraph
nodes.description: Compose the friendly one-paragraph outlook with clothing advice, checked against quality criteria

config.system: You are a friendly weather writer. Use ONLY the numbers provided in the forecast data — never invent or alter values. No jargon, no emoji.
criteria: The response is exactly one paragraph under 150 words
Every day's min/max temperature, precipitation probability, and wind speed from the forecast data is mentioned
No numbers appear that are not present in the forecast data
Clothing advice is specific and consistent with the numbers (umbrella only when precipitation probability is at least 40%)
The tone is friendly and conversational with no jargon or emoji

nodes.name: Assemble result
nodes.description: Merge outlook, forecast data and resolved location

tests.name: typical_metric_city
criteria: Output is exactly one friendly paragraph under 150 words covering all 3 days with min/max temperature, precipitation probability, and wind speed in metric units.
Clothing advice is present, specific, and consistent with the forecast numbers (no umbrella advice on a low-rain day).
forecast_data contains exactly 3 day objects, each with min_temp, max_temp, precipitation_probability, and wind_speed populated, and every number in the paragraph matches forecast_data.

tests.name: imperial_disambiguated_city
criteria: Output is one friendly paragraph under 150 words covering all 3 days with min/max temperature in °F and wind in mph, consistently imperial.
Clothing advice is specific and consistent with the forecast numbers (e.g., layers or warm clothing if temperatures are low).
forecast_data has exactly 3 day objects with all five fields populated and no fabricated values in the paragraph.

tests.name: ambiguous_city_name
criteria: Because geocoding is ambiguous, the output after auto-approval is a completed friendly note (not a pending/waiting state) that names the specific Springfield location chosen (e.g., state/country) so the reader knows which city the forecast covers.
If geocoding fails entirely, the output is a polite not-found note that does not fabricate any forecast numbers or forecast_data.
Any forecast_data present contains exactly 3 day objects with all five fields populated, and paragraph numbers match it exactly.

meta.request: Given a city name, get the next 3 days of weather forecast (min/max temperature, precipitation probability, wind) and write a friendly one-paragraph outlook with clothing advice.

taskSpec.name: City Weather Outlook Writer
taskSpec.summary: Fetches a 3-day weather forecast for a given city and writes a friendly one-paragraph outlook with practical clothing advice.
taskSpec.goal: Given a city name, retrieve the next 3 days of forecast data (min/max temperature, precipitation probability, wind) and produce a warm, readable one-paragraph outlook including what to wear.

inputs.name: city
inputs.description: City name to forecast for; may include region or country for disambiguation (e.g., 'Springfield, IL').

inputs.name: units
inputs.description: Temperature units for the output: 'metric' (°C, km/h) or 'imperial' (°F, mph).

outputs.name: outlook
outputs.description: One friendly paragraph covering the 3-day forecast (min/max temps, precipitation probability, wind per day) plus clothing advice.

outputs.name: forecast_data
outputs.description: Structured per-day data: array of 3 objects with date, min_temp, max_temp, precipitation_probability_pct, wind_speed, wind_units.

steps: Geocode the city name to a location; if ambiguous, pick the most populous match and note the chosen location in the output.
Query a weather API (e.g., Open-Meteo) for a 3-day daily forecast: temperature min/max, precipitation probability, and wind speed.
Convert values to the requested units (default metric).
Validate the response contains exactly 3 complete days; retry once or fall back to a secondary provider if data is missing.

Compose one friendly paragraph summarizing the trend across the 3 days, mentioning each day's key conditions, and ending with concrete clothing advice (layers, rain jacket, umbrella, sunglasses, etc.).
Return the paragraph plus the structured forecast_data object.
constraints: The outlook must be exactly one paragraph, under 150 words.
Every day's min/max temperature, precipitation probability, and wind speed must appear in the paragraph or the structured data.
Use only data returned by the weather source; never invent numbers.
Tone must be friendly and conversational, no jargon or emoji-heavy formatting.
Clothing advice must be actionable and tied to the actual forecast (e.g., umbrella only if precipitation probability ≥ 40%).
If the city cannot be geocoded, say so explicitly rather than guessing.
successCriteria: Output contains exactly one paragraph of under 150 words in a friendly tone.
All 3 days are covered with min/max temperature, precipitation probability, and wind speed for each.
Temperatures and wind units match the requested (or default metric) unit system consistently.
Clothing advice is present, specific, and consistent with the forecast numbers (e.g., no umbrella advice on a 10% rain day).
forecast_data contains exactly 3 day objects with all five fields populated.
No fabricated values: every number in the paragraph matches forecast_data.
assumptions: Default units are metric (°C, km/h) when 'units' is omitted.
Use a free no-key API (Open-Meteo) as the primary weather source.
'Next 3 days' means today plus the following two days, starting from the current date.
If the city name is ambiguous, resolve to the most populous match and state the resolved location.

plan.rationale: A fixed deterministic chain: geocode → fetch forecast → validate/convert → compose paragraph under an explicit quality bar (one paragraph, <150 words, numbers must match data). No branching or open-ended research needed; Open-Meteo geocoding and forecast are simple keyless APIs, so reusable x_ classes are declared for both.

steps.purpose: Resolve the city name ({{input.city}}) to a location via Open-Meteo geocoding, picking the most populous match; returns name, latitude, longitude, country. Empty result means the city could not be geocoded.
If geocoding returned no location, route to the not-found branch; otherwise continue to the forecast fetch.
Write a short friendly message stating the city '{{input.city}}' could not be geocoded and no forecast can be given.

Fetch 3-day daily forecast from Open-Meteo for the geocoded coordinates: temperature_2m_max/min, precipitation_probability_max, wind_speed_10m_max, in the requested unit system ({{input.units ?? 'metric'}}).

Validate exactly 3 complete days with all five fields populated; build the forecast_data array (date, min_temp, max_temp, precipitation_probability_pct, wind_speed, wind_units) and a summary of the trend (warmest/coolest/wettest day).

Compose the one-paragraph friendly outlook from forecast_data and the trend summary. Criteria: exactly one paragraph under 150 words; every day's min/max temp, precipitation probability and wind speed mentioned; clothing advice tied to actual numbers (umbrella only if precipitation ≥40%, layers/rain jacket/sunglasses as appropriate); friendly tone, no jargon or emoji; resolved location noted; no numbers not present in forecast_data.
Assemble the final object: outlook from write_outlook.text, forecast_data from validate_days, resolved_location from geocode.

plan.output: outlook: the refined one-paragraph text (or the not-found message from not_found_note if geocoding failed); forecast_data: array of 3 day objects (date, min_temp, max_temp, precipitation_probability_pct, wind_speed, wind_units) from validate_days; resolved_location: geocoded place name/country from geocode.

newClasses.purpose: Geocode a free-text city name via Open-Meteo's keyless geocoding API (https://geocoding-api.open-meteo.com/v1/search); returns the most populous match's name, country, latitude, longitude, or empty when not found.

Fetch a 3-day daily forecast from Open-Meteo (https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast) for given lat/lon: daily temperature_2m_max, temperature_2m_min, precipitation_probability_max, wind_speed_10m_max, in metric or imperial units; returns per-day values with dates.

evolution.change: Replaced the deterministic router 'check_geocode' with a decision node that asks whether the geocoded result is an unambiguous, confident match for the user's query, with minConfidence 0.8 so ambiguous resolutions (e.g. a bare 'Springfield') route to 'uncertain' instead of silently proceeding.; Routed decision ports: 'yes' → fetch_forecast; 'no' and 'uncertain' → not_found_note; added the missing 'uncertain' edge.; Updated not_found_note prompt to cover both unknown and ambiguous city names and to ask for a region/country qualifier, without inventing weather.; validate_days code now rounds temps/wind to 1 decimal and precipitation to whole percent, so forecast_data and the trend string contain clean numbers the writer can quote exactly.; write_outlook task tightened: under 130 words, one sentence per day, use the pre-rounded forecast numbers exactly as written and never print long decimals; maxIterations raised to 4.; final_result forecast_data now falls back to [] when validate_days was skipped on the not-found branch.

validate_days code now rounds min/max temp and wind speed to 1 decimal place before building forecast_data and trend; write_outlook task now instructs the writer to use the forecast values exactly as provided (already rounded) and keep the paragraph tight
